title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 21
statement: Let \(N\) be a three-digit integer such that the difference between any two positive integer factors of \(N\) is divisible by 3 . Let \(d(N)\) denote the number of positive integers which divide \(N\). Find the maximum possible value of \(N \cdot d(N)\).

solutions.text: 5586 We first note that all the prime factors of \(n\) must be 1 modulo 3 (and thus 1 modulo 6 ). The smallest primes with this property are \(7,13,19, \ldots\). Since \(7^{4}=2401>1000\), the number can have at most 3 prime factors (including repeats). Since \(7 \cdot 13 \cdot 19=1729>1000\), the most factors \(N\) can have is 6 . Consider the number \(7^{2} \cdot 19=931\), which has 6 factors. For this choice of \(N, N \cdot d(N)=5586\). For another \(N\) to do better, it must have at least 6 factors, for otherwise, \(N \cdot d(N)<1000 \cdot 5=5000\). It is easy to verify that \(7^{2} \cdot 19\) is the greatest number with 6 prime factors satisfying our conditions, so the answer must be 5586 .
